content: Oliver's sign refers to an abnormal downward movement of the trachea during the systolic phase of the cardiac cycle. This clinical finding may suggest the presence of a dilation or aneurysm of the aortic arch. If an aneurysm is present, the anatomical relationship of the aortic arch, which lies above the left main bronchus, may cause a downward tugging sensation of the trachea. This sign was first described in 1878 by William Silver Oliver, an English military surgeon. The potential causes of Oliver's sign include life-threatening conditions that require immediate medical attention, as they may result in death or irreversible damage within 24 hours if untreated. These include an aortic aneurysm and aortic dissection. Other common causes of Oliver's sign include: Aortic aneurysm Aortic dissection Atherosclerosis Cystic medial necrosis Marfan's syndrome Trauma
